page.layout: One printed page, text only. Top: page number 356 at the left and running head "DE MUSICA." centred. Below, a centred heading "Quot sunt Claves?" with a diagram: at left a brace listing the seven clefs with "Præcipuè", at centre "G, C, F, signantur in cantu choralí sic:" with a musical staff, at right "In figurali vero sic:" with a second staff. Full-width line "Si cantus b mollis est: Sin cantus □ durus." Then a two-column table of solmisation with the label "Canitur in" at left. Then the headings and paragraphs "Quid est Vox?", "Quot sunt voces?", "Quid est Mutatio?" and "Quid est Figura?", each followed by italic text. No margin notes. No bottom text.

main_text.head: Quot sunt Claves?
main_text.l: G, C, F, signantur in cantu choralí sic:

p.i: Si cantus b mollis est: Sin cantus □ durus.

main_text.head: Quid est Vox?

p.i: Vox est qua clavium tenor exprimitur.

main_text.head: Quot sunt voces?

p.i: Sex: ut, re, mi, fa, sol, la.

main_text.head: Quid est Mutatio?

p.i: Mutatio est vocis in vocem in eadem clave unisona variatio. Omnis mutatio Ascendendo fit per Re: Descendendo vero per La.

main_text.head: Quid est Figura?

p.i: Figura est signū vocis aut silentii. Si-gnum

page.notes: The two musical staves under "sic:" are printed music notation (clef and note symbols) and are not transcribed; they are described only as staves. The "□" signs are the printed natural and square-b signs. The "Canitur in" table header and the italic "Descend." and "Ascend." labels are copied as printed. The Greek-style "Re" and "La" in the Mutatio sentence are printed in a script face and are copied as printed.
